text:
Camila Reyes: Kicking off deck template refresh thread here. Goal: consistent visuals for latency/cost across the demo deck (charts, callouts, icons). We’re getting mixed styles in v1 and it looks stitched together.

Soojin Lee: +1. Specific pain: the “production economics” section has 3 different chart styles (one looks like product UI, one looks like a blog chart, one looks like a vendor benchmark slide). We need a single visual language.

Iris Chen: Got it. Can you point me to the current source deck + where the worst offenders are? (Slides numbers help.)

Camila Reyes: Here’s the working file (internal): https://drive.google.com/redwood/demo-deck-outline-working
- Slide 8 “Latency vs cost tradeoffs”
- Slide 9 “Token-level breakdown”
- Slide 12 “Caching win”
- Appendix: “Dedicated economics” chart

Jordan Park: Adding: we should standardize the “callout pill” style too (today there’s rounded blue pills + sharp orange tags).

Soojin Lee: Re: style direction: I’d like it to feel “product-adjacent” but not literally screenshots. Like: crisp, minimal, engineering-friendly. Not hype.

Iris Chen: Proposal (rough):
1) Charts: single style for all perf/cost charts (2px stroke, muted gridlines, one accent color per metric).
2) Latency = teal, Cost = orange, Reliability = purple (consistent across deck).
3) Use the same axis labeling + units everywhere (ms, $/1M tokens).

Camila Reyes: Love the color mapping. But careful on orange — our current brand orange is loud and reads “warning.” Can we do an amber that still feels positive?

Iris Chen: Yep. I’ll pick an amber that passes contrast + doesn’t scream error. We can keep error states as red.

Elliot Price: +1 on units. Also we keep flipping between “$/M tok” and “$/1M tokens” and it confuses people when we narrate live.

Jordan Park: Another thing: the “token-level breakdown” slide currently has 6 tiny segments and is unreadable on Zoom. Can we make it a simplified stacked bar + 2–3 callouts?

Soojin Lee: Agree. We should optimize for being readable at 80% size, Zoom compression, and screenshare. The segment detail can go in speaker notes.

Camila Reyes: Guardrail: any benchmark-like charts need a “example / illustrative” label unless eng has explicitly blessed numbers. We’ve been asked to avoid precise competitor deltas.

Iris Chen: Understood. We can make the charts “shape-forward” (relative improvements) and use ranges / placeholders. Ex: “20–35% lower p95” rather than “28.7%”.

Markus Klein: Jumping in from SE side — in the live demo we’ll reference these visuals while Console graphs are on-screen. If the slide charts look totally different from Console it feels weird.

Iris Chen: Makes sense. I can mirror Console’s general aesthetic (light grid, thin lines) without copying UI exactly. We’ll keep the deck consistent and not “UI screenshot soup.”

Soojin Lee: Also: iconography. Right now we’ve got mixed icon sets (outline vs filled, different corner radii). Can design define a mini set just for this deck? (Compute/GPU, Routing, Cache, Shield, Graph.)

Jordan Park: I can pull a cohesive outline set and normalize stroke widths. We’ll export as SVG + embed in Slides.

Camila Reyes: :thumbsup: What’s the output format? We need something reps can copy without breaking.

Iris Chen: Plan:
- Figma: master templates (title, section divider, standard 2-col, chart slide, appendix).
- Google Slides: a “locked-ish” template deck using those components.
- Small style guide page: colors, chart rules, icon rules, spacing.

Elliot Price: Please include “do / don’t” for charts (e.g., don’t add 3D, don’t use rainbow, don’t use screenshots of random Datadog graphs).

Soojin Lee: Timing: can we get v0 by EOW? We need to review before the next enablement session.

Iris Chen: EOW is tight but doable for v0. Scope for v0:
- New template slides
- Rebuild slide 8 and 9 (latency/cost + token breakdown)
- Icon set
Then v1 next week to rebuild the rest.

Camila Reyes: Works. Can we align on a few specifics now?
1) Typeface: keep current deck font or switch?
2) Background: pure white vs slightly off-white?

Iris Chen: Typeface: keep Inter (matches product) unless there’s a strong reason to change. Background: slight off-white so charts don’t feel floating; but it needs to print OK.

Soojin Lee: Inter is good. For background, off-white is fine as long as it doesn’t look “beige” on projectors.

Jordan Park: I’ll test on dark projector mode + Zoom share. We can set a super subtle #F8FAFC.

Camila Reyes: Great. Please drop Figma link here when ready + tag @Soojin Lee and me for async review.

Iris Chen: Will do. I’ll also add a “Latency vs Cost” component that’s re-usable so we stop re-drawing charts per slide.

Markus Klein: One request: add a “backup screenshot framing” style (same border + caption) for when we fall back to static Console screenshots.

Iris Chen: Good call. I’ll add a screenshot frame component (caption + redaction note area).

Camila Reyes: :white_check_mark: Thank you. Action items:
- Iris: draft templates + rebuild slides 8/9 + screenshot frame (EOW)
- Jordan: icon set + chart spec doc snippet
- Soojin/Camila: review + confirm copy labels (“illustrative”, units)

Soojin Lee: Thanks all. When we review, we should check the “production economics” headline slide too — if the visuals get more disciplined, we might need to simplify copy to match.

Iris Chen: Agreed. I’ll keep plenty of whitespace so we’re not tempted to cram.
